verdict.rationale: First-party Graph docs document a driveItem delta endpoint that tracks changes to a driveItem and its children over time. Delta query is described as letting apps discover created, updated, or deleted entities without a full read on every request, which is the core of this story. Missing for 10: the cursor/token mechanics (e.g., how the state token is returned and reused across calls) are not shown in the evidence, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can sync efficiently — a cursor/delta endpoint returns only what changed since my last call instead of forcing a full re-crawl

citations.quote: Track changes in a driveItem and its children over time.
Delta query, also called change tracking, enables applications to discover newly created, updated, or deleted entities without performing a full read of the target resource with every request.
